answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by making trust depend on escrowed deposits and randomized cross-checks: a trellis of trusted agents challenges each newcomer on tasks, then accepts it only after peers sign a cipher-protected record of useful work. Creating fake identities requires an attacker to lock capital, perform costly work, and recruit unrelated endorsers for every identity; failed checks slash deposits, so multiplying aliases becomes a steep dune of expense rather than a cheap vote.
